data.name: get_patterns
data.text:
## menu — Menu (component, archetype navigate)
A transient list of choices or commands revealed from a trigger.
Aliases: dropdown menu, context menu, overflow menu, menu bar, mega menu
Anatomy: Trigger (What opens the menu); Items (Choices and commands); Structure (Sections and submenus)
Related — neighbors: command-palette, popover
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Opening [invocation] — What opens it?
  - openBy (single-select: one id) — Opened by
      button-click: Button click (e.g. Overflow ⋮ menus)
      right-click-or-long-press: Right-click or long-press (e.g. Context menus)
      menu-bar: Menu bar (e.g. macOS menu bar)
      hover: Hover (e.g. Retail mega menus)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. Alt to reach Windows menus)
* Structure [composition] — How are items organized?
  - structure (single-select: one id) — Structure
      flat: Flat (e.g. Overflow menus)
      sections: Sections (e.g. Google Docs menus)
      cascading-submenus: Cascading submenus (e.g. Desktop menu bars)
      mega-menu: Mega menu — Multi-column panel (e.g. Retail department menus)
* Item content [content] — What does each item show?
  - item (multi-select: list of ids) — Item content
      label: Label (e.g. All)
      icon: Icon (e.g. Google Docs)
      shortcut-hint: Shortcut hint (e.g. macOS menus)
      checkmark-state: Checkmark state (e.g. View menus)
      description: Description (e.g. GitHub menus)
* Item set [initiative] — Who decides which items appear and in what order?
  - itemSet (single-select: one id) — Item set
      fixed: Fixed (e.g. Most menus)
      depends-on-selection: Depends on selection (e.g. Context menus)
      adaptive: Adaptive — The system reorders by use (e.g. Office 2000 personalized menus)
      adaptable: Adaptable — The person reorders (e.g. Office Quick Access Toolbar)
* Form [layout] — What shape is it?
  - form (single-select: one id) — Form
      vertical-list: Vertical list (e.g. Most menus)
      radial: Radial (e.g. Blender pie menus)
      icon-grid: Icon grid (e.g. Google apps launcher)
      horizontal-bar: Horizontal bar (e.g. Toolbars)

## banner — Banner (component, archetype monitor)
A persistent message across a region or page about a condition that needs attention.
Aliases: inline alert, callout, system banner, notice
Anatomy: Message (The condition); Severity (How serious); Action (What to do); Dismiss (Whether it can go away)
Related — neighbors: toast, empty-state
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Scope [scope] — What does the condition apply to?
  - scope (single-select: one id) — Scope
      whole-app: Whole app (e.g. Service outage banners)
      page: Page (e.g. Account warnings)
      section: Section (e.g. GOV.UK error summary)
      field: Field (e.g. Inline field notices)
* Severity [feedback] — How serious is it?
  - severity (single-select: one id) — Severity
      information: Information (e.g. Scheduled maintenance)
      success: Success (e.g. Settings saved)
      warning: Warning (e.g. Card expiring)
      critical: Critical (e.g. Payment failed)
* Dismissal [lifecycle] — Can it go away?
  - dismissal (single-select: one id) — Dismissal
      not-until-resolved: Not until resolved (e.g. Verification required)
      dismissible: Dismissible (e.g. Announcements)
      returns-later: Returns later (e.g. Update reminders)
      clears-with-the-condition: Clears with the condition (e.g. Connectivity banners)
* Action [content] — Does it offer a way to fix things?
  - action (single-select: one id) — Action
      none: None (e.g. Maintenance notices)
      link-to-fix: Link to fix (e.g. Update payment method)
      primary-action: Primary action (e.g. Restart to update)
      several-actions: Several actions (e.g. Cookie consent)
* Placement [layout] — Where does it sit?
  - placement (single-select: one id) — Placement
      top-of-the-app: Top of the app (e.g. GitHub site-wide banners)
      top-of-content: Top of cont

data.name: get_patterns
data.text:
## carousel — Carousel (component, archetype browse-collections)
A horizontally scrolling strip that shows a subset of items at once and hides the rest off-screen.
Aliases: slider, shelf, horizontal scroller
Anatomy: Track (The items in order); Viewport (What is currently visible); Controls (Arrows, dots, swipe)
Related — uses: card, pagination | neighbors: stories, tabs
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Visible items [layout] — How many items are visible, and how?
  - visible (single-select: one id) — Visible items
      one-at-a-time: One at a time — A hero slide (e.g. Homepage hero carousels)
      peek-next: Peek next — The next item shows at the edge (e.g. App Store)
      multi-item-strip: Multi-item strip (e.g. Netflix rows)
      hero-with-smaller-neighbours: Hero with smaller neighbours (e.g. Material 3 hero carousel)
* Advancing [invocation] — How does it move?
  - advance (multi-select: list of ids) — Advance by
      swipe: Swipe (e.g. Mobile)
      arrow-buttons: Arrow buttons (e.g. Netflix on web)
      dots: Dots (e.g. Hero banners)
      autoplay: Autoplay (e.g. Marketing heroes)
* Timing [lifecycle] — Does it move on its own?
  - autoplay (single-select: one id) — Autoplay
      off: Off (e.g. Netflix)
      timed-pausing-on-interaction: Timed, pausing on interaction (e.g. Retail heroes)
      continuous-marquee: Continuous marquee (e.g. Logo walls)
* Position [feedback] — Does it say where you are?
  - indicator (single-select: one id) — Position indicator
      none: None (e.g. Netflix rows)
      dots: Dots (e.g. Hero banners)
      counter: Counter — 3 of 10 (e.g. Product image galleries)
      progress-bar: Progress bar (e.g. Stories)

## media-player — Media player (pattern, archetype consume-media)
A stage and transport for playing video or audio, with position, quality and optional overlays under the person’s control.
Aliases: video player, audio player, playback controls
Anatomy: Stage (Where the media renders); Transport bar (Play, seek, volume); Chrome (Title, creator and actions); Overlays (Captions, chapters, ads)
Related — uses: slider, menu, toast, progress-indicator | specializes: consume-media | neighbors: playlist-queue, timeline-editor
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Transport controls [flow] — Which playback controls are available?
  - controls (multi-select: list of ids) — Controls
      play-pause: Play pause (e.g. YouTube)
      scrubber: Scrubber (e.g. Netflix)
      skip-forward-back: Skip forward back (e.g. Apple Podcasts ±15s)
      playback-speed: Playback speed (e.g. YouTube speed menu)
      volume-and-mute: Volume and mute (e.g. Spotify)
      fullscreen: Fullscreen (e.g. Vimeo)
* Position and chapters [content] — How is position shown and segmented?
  - position (multi-select: list of ids) — Position encoding
      time-scrubber: Time scrubber (e.g. YouTube)
      chapter-markers: Chapter markers (e.g. YouTube chapters)
      heatmap-of-rewatches: Heatmap of rewatches (e.g. YouTube most-replayed)
      lyrics-synced-to-time: Lyrics synced to time (e.g. Spotify Lyrics)
      thumbnail-previews-on-hover: Thumbnail previews on hover (e.g. YouTube scrub previews)
* Presentation mode [layout] — How is the player framed on screen?
  - mode (single-select: one id) — Mode
      inline-embed: Inline embed (e.g. YouTube on news sites)
      theater-or-immersive: Theater or immersive (e.g. YouTube Theater)
      fullscreen: Fullscreen (e.g. Netflix)
      mini-or-pip: Mini or PiP (e.g. YouTube PiP)
      lock-screen-now-playing: Lock-screen / Now Playing (e.g. iOS Now Playing)
      standalone-window: Standalone window — A desktop player in its own resizable window, neither embedded in a page nor fullscreen by default (e.g. VLC — Desktop player)
* Adaptation [adaptation] — How does playback adapt to device and network?
  - adaptation (multi-select: list of ids) — Adaptation
      adaptive-bitrate: Adaptive bitrate (e.g. Netflix
